originality.rationale: The foundational full text, the strongest same-object energy paper, and a modern mathematical treatment were compared at statement/implication level. The energy paper supplies a global scalar balance, not localization against arbitrary observables of y or z. Targeted exact-object searches found no same-object conditional-nullcline or variance-speed theorem. The accepted novelty is restricted to those localized stationary laws, their exact derivative-energy defects, and equality rigidity.
residual_risks: The accepted identities are algebraically short, so a differently phrased incidental observation in unindexed neuroscience, control, or synchronization literature could remain unlocated.
Stochastic Hindmarsh–Rose stationary distributions are a different object and were not treated as coverage of the deterministic invariant-measure theorem.
The energy literature contains global average balances; future comparisons should continue to distinguish those from the coordinatewise conditional identities accepted here.
The theorem does not assert existence of a non-equilibrium compact invariant measure for every parameter choice.

value.rationale: The fast recovery and slow adaptation coordinates are the organizing variables of the Hindmarsh–Rose bursting mechanism. The theorem determines voltage power separately at every fast-recovery level and mean voltage separately at every slow-adaptation level, then identifies the unexplained variance exactly with mean-square recovery or adaptation speed. This supplies exact stationary consistency diagnostics for a canonical bursting-neuron benchmark and rigorously distinguishes equilibrium-supported statistics from genuinely time-dependent spiking or bursting states. It is structurally finer than a global time-averaged energy balance and is not a numerical recomputation of firing rates or Lyapunov exponents.
